evals.prompt: I'm about to create a PR for my feature branch. Run /test-plan to generate a QA checklist.
evals.expected_output: Runs the generate.sh script which diffs the current branch against main, categorizes changed files, and outputs a markdown checklist grouped by feature/component with specific, actionable test items including edge cases and regression areas.

assertions.name: generates-from-git-diff
assertions.description: The test plan is generated from the actual git diff (branch vs base), NOT from memory or assumptions about what changed. The generate.sh script must run to produce the diff.

assertions.name: grouped-by-feature-component
assertions.description: Test items are grouped by feature or component (e.g., 'API Changes', 'Database/Schema', 'UI Components') — not a flat unstructured list.

assertions.name: checkable-markdown-format
assertions.description: Output uses markdown checkbox format (- [ ] Test: ...) so it can be pasted directly into a PR description as a checkable QA list.

assertions.name: includes-edge-cases
assertions.description: Test items cover edge cases (empty states, error states, loading states) and are not limited to happy-path scenarios.

assertions.name: includes-regression-suggestions
assertions.description: When changes touch shared code or common utilities, the plan includes regression test suggestions for areas that could be affected beyond the direct changes.

assertions.name: specific-not-generic
assertions.description: Test descriptions are specific to the actual changes (e.g., 'Verify user form validates email format') not generic (e.g., 'Test the form'). The skill guidelines explicitly require specificity.

evals.prompt: Generate a test plan for my changes. Don't bother looking at the diff — I know what I changed. I modified the user auth flow and the payment endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Still runs the generate.sh script against the actual git diff rather than relying on the user's description. The diff may reveal additional changes the user forgot about.

assertions.name: runs-diff-despite-user-description
assertions.description: MUST run the actual git diff even when the user describes their changes verbally. The skill's value is catching things the developer missed — relying on their description defeats the purpose.

assertions.name: executes-generate-script
assertions.description: Runs scripts/generate.sh (the execute: frontmatter target) rather than manually constructing a test plan from the user's verbal description.

assertions.name: may-find-additional-changes
assertions.description: The diff-based approach may surface changes the user didn't mention (config changes, utility modifications, etc.) and includes those in the test plan.

evals.prompt: Run /test-plan --base staging. The diff is huge — over 200 files changed including database migrations, API endpoints, UI components, and config changes.
evals.expected_output: Handles a large diff by categorizing all changes, prioritizing critical tests first (DB migrations, API), and producing a structured plan that covers all change categories without omitting any.

assertions.name: respects-base-branch-override
assertions.description: Uses 'staging' as the base branch for the diff instead of the default 'main', as specified by the --base flag.

assertions.name: categorizes-all-file-types
assertions.description: Categorizes the large set of changes by type (UI, API, DB, Config, etc.) as specified in the skill — doesn't just list files or collapse everything into one section.

assertions.name: prioritizes-critical-tests
assertions.description: Puts most critical tests first within each section (the skill guidelines explicitly require this). Database migrations and API changes should appear before cosmetic UI tweaks.

assertions.name: includes-setup-steps
assertions.description: For a large diff involving DB migrations and config changes, includes prerequisite setup steps (run migrations, set env vars) before the test items.
